subsystems.name: Qubit chip
subsystems.role: the processor itself — a millimetre-scale silicon or sapphire die carrying tens to hundreds of qubits.

subsystems.name: Josephson junctions
subsystems.role: the non-linear element that makes a circuit behave like an artificial atom with distinct energy levels.

subsystems.name: Cryogenics
subsystems.role: cools the chip to around 10–20 millikelvin, where the circuits become superconducting and thermal noise disappears.

subsystems.name: Control and readout electronics
subsystems.role: generate the microwave pulses that drive gates and interpret the faint signals coming back.

subsystems.name: Shielding and filtering
subsystems.role: keeps stray heat, infrared light and magnetic fields from destroying the quantum state.

subsystems.name: Wiring and packaging
subsystems.role: carries hundreds of control lines from room temperature down to the chip without overheating the fridge.

buildSteps.title: Grow and clean the substrate
buildSteps.detail: A high-purity silicon or sapphire wafer is polished and cleaned so films will grow with very few defects — defects cause qubit decoherence.

buildSteps.title: Deposit superconducting films
buildSteps.detail: Niobium or aluminium is deposited by sputtering or evaporation, then patterned with photolithography and etching to form resonators and wiring.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate Josephson junctions
buildSteps.detail: A shadow-evaporation technique — often the Dolan bridge — lays down one aluminium electrode, oxidises its surface to form a nanometre-thin barrier, then lays down the second electrode at a different angle.

buildSteps.title: Dice and mount the chip
buildSteps.detail: The wafer is diced and the chip wire-bonded into a shielded sample package with well-controlled microwave ports.

buildSteps.title: Wire the cryostat
buildSteps.detail: The package is mounted at the coldest stage of a dilution refrigerator, with carefully attenuated and filtered lines for every qubit and readout channel.

buildSteps.title: Cool down
buildSteps.detail: Over roughly a day the fridge steps down through several temperature stages to millikelvin, and the metal films become superconducting.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the qubits
buildSteps.detail: Each qubit's frequency, pulse amplitudes and readout thresholds are measured and tuned; cross-talk between neighbours is characterised.

buildSteps.title: Run gates and correct errors
buildSteps.detail: Single- and two-qubit gates are executed, measured, and repeated in error-correcting cycles that combine many physical qubits into one more reliable logical qubit.

prerequisites.why: superconducting qubits only behave quantum-mechanically near absolute zero, and the fridge must cool hundreds of wires without adding noise.
junction barriers a nanometre thick must be uniform, or qubits vary too much to control.
gates are microwave pulses, and reading a single qubit requires amplifiers near the quantum limit.
physical qubits are too error-prone alone; many must be combined into one logical qubit, and this has been shown to work better as the code grows only recently.
thousands of room-temperature cables per chip do not scale; control must move into the fridge.

pathway.milestone: cloud-accessible processors with tens to a few hundred noisy physical qubits
pathway.unlocks: early experiments in quantum simulation, optimisation and algorithm research.

pathway.milestone: error-corrected logical qubits that clearly outperform the best physical ones
pathway.unlocks: longer, more reliable circuits than any single qubit could run.

pathway.milestone: machines with hundreds of logical qubits, wired and controlled in three dimensions
pathway.unlocks: quantum chemistry and materials problems beyond classical simulation.

pathway.milestone: fault-tolerant processors running millions of gate operations
pathway.unlocks: practical attacks on some cryptography and design of new catalysts and drugs.
